place.source_title: Detroit Lakes Public Library, 1000 Washington Avenue

brief: Carnegie-funded Prairie School public library: a low one-and-a-half-storey block of dark tapestry brick on a raised basement under a broad hipped tile-look roof with deep overhanging eaves, bands of tall windows with light stone sills and trim, a projecting entrance bay with stone piers, and a tall brick chimney; a later one-storey hip-roofed addition at the side, set on a lawn.

facade.notes: the Detroit Lakes MN Carnegie library (1913), HABS: a low Prairie School block of dark tapestry brick on a raised basement, broad hipped tile roof with deep eaves, ribbon windows, a projecting entrance bay with stone trim; a later low hipped addition behind

why.note: Carnegie grants (1883-1919) built most small-town libraries: one storey over a raised basement, a central entrance, the town paying the site and upkeep
Prairie School libraries of the upper Midwest, 1905-1920
